summary: STARFORGE is an immersive single-player space mission simulation game that merges systems engineering with tactical planetary exploration. It addresses the challenge of complex aerospace design by requiring players to manage a shared global budget across five modular laboratories, carefully balancing critical trade-offs among mass, round-trip fuel capacity, and technology levels. The project is important because it promotes STEM education, critical thinking, and strategic problem-solving, demonstrating how real-world engineering constraints and physical limits impact mission success.
details:
STARFORGE: Project Overview

1. What it does and how it works

STARFORGE is a single-player space mission simulation gamewhere you step into the shoes of an aerospace engineer under pressure. It blends deep systems engineering with hands-on gameplay across two main stages:

  • Phase 1 (The Progressive NASA Base & Hangar): You start with a nearly empty base—just some grass, old landing strips, and a central launch pad. Using a shared global budget, you build out five modular labs piece by piece. Every component choice forces a trade-off between weight, cost, and technology level. Before you can even think about launching, your rocket and rover must pass rigorous physics checks for mass, thrust-to-weight ratios, and round-trip fuel capacity.
  • Phase 2 (Tactical Planetary Exploration): Once you successfully reach the Moon, the game shifts into a tactical RTS-style experience. You command your custom rover across the harsh, crater-filled terrain of the lunar South Pole using click-to-move controls. You'll have to manage your battery life, dodge thermal overheating in rocky fields, and navigate the dangerous contrast between blinding solar heat and freezing dark craters.

2. Benefits offered

  • Gamified Engineering: It turns complex aerospace concepts—like mission design labs, weight limits, and fuel margins—into an intuitive puzzle that is actually fun to solve.
  • Critical Thinking: It breaks the habit of "mindless optimization." Players quickly learn that always picking the cheapest, lightest part will backfire because low-tech gear yields useless scientific data or faulty navigation.
  • Immersive Progression: Seeing your base expand and your rover visually transform as you install new parts makes every milestone feel deeply earned.

3. Intended impact

Our goal with STARFORGE is to spark a genuine fascination for STEM fields and space exploration. By showing players the real-world friction of balancing budgets, physics, and scientific value under tight constraints, we want to inspire the next generation of problem-solvers and engineers.

4. Tools, programming languages, hardware, and software used

  • Game Engine: Godot 4.3+ (GDScript).
  • Visual Style: Fluid 2D Pixel Art built on a 640x360 base resolution (canvas_items, Nearest neighbor filtering), enhanced with dynamic 2D lighting shaders and particle systems (GPUParticles2D).
  • Audio Design: An adaptive, Hans Zimmer-inspired dynamic soundtrack (AudioStreamSynchronized) that shifts from minimalist space ambient to heart-pounding launch climaxes.
  • Architecture: A clean modular codebase separated into core logic rules, exploration systems, renderers, and automated test suites.

5. Creative aspects

  • 1994 Retro Aesthetic: We leaned heavily into an old-school computer vibe complete with CRT scanlines and terminal-style briefings.
  • Midnight Club-Style Customization: In the hangar, every part you choose instantly changes the visual sprite of your rover and rocket in real-time, giving you that satisfying "tuning garage" feeling.
  • The Sarcastic Virtual Guide: Instead of boring text pop-ups, you have a caffeinated, cynical veteran engineer guiding you. He delivers mission briefings via a typewriter effect and reacts live on a side panel during gameplay, roasting you with witty humor whenever your rover overheats or your rocket turns into fireworks.

6. Key considerations by the team

  • The "Cheap Part" Trap: We wanted to avoid a meta where players just min-max the lightest parts. Introducing the Tech Level system meant that cheap, low-tech parts actively sabotage your scientific mission, forcing genuine strategic compromise.
  • Real Physics Constraints: Implementing strict round-trip fuel calculations ensures that sloppy building leads to catastrophic launch failures, teaching players respect for real orbital mechanics.
  • High-Stakes Survival Mechanics: Features like the thermal light/shadow cycle and the panic Emergency Purge button (which vents heat instantly at the cost of 15% battery) were designed to create breathless, cinematic moments of tension and relief.
